source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which pair of findings does the nurse expect in a client with end-stage renal disease?
questions.rationale: The kidneys maintain water balance and secrete erythropoietin, which stimulates red cell production. When they fail, edema and anemia result.
explanations: Oliguria and tachycardia are more likely.
Correct: lost water balance and erythropoietin.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q175 (PDF p. 328)
questions.quote: Impairment of these functions results in edema and anemia.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client is admitted with acute glomerulonephritis. Which recent history should the nurse ask about?
questions.rationale: The main cause of acute glomerulonephritis is a beta-hemolytic streptococcal infection about 3 weeks before symptoms begin, such as strep throat or impetigo.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q177 (PDF p. 330)
questions.quote: The predominant cause of acute glomerulonephritis is infection with beta-hemolytic Streptococcus 3 weeks before the onset of symptoms.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which parameter should the nurse check DAILY in a client with nephrotic syndrome?
questions.rationale: Nephrotic syndrome causes edema, hypoalbuminemia, and proteinuria. Fluid balance is tracked daily by weight, intake and output, edema, and girth. Albumin is checked as prescribed.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q183 (PDF p. 336)
questions.quote: The nurse carefully assesses the fluid balance of the client, which includes daily monitoring of weight, intake and output, edema, and girth measurements.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which item should be kept in the room of a client being evaluated for the type of kidney stone?
questions.rationale: Urine is strained until the stone passes. The stone is sent to the laboratory, and once its type is known, a prevention plan is made.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q271 (PDF p. 428)
questions.quote: Straining the urine will catch small stones that should be sent to the laboratory for analysis.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the MOST serious complication of polycystic kidney disease?
questions.rationale: Cysts form and the kidneys enlarge. The most serious complication is ESRD, managed by dialysis or transplant. Chronic UTI is the most common complication.
explanations: The most common, not the most serious.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q363 (PDF p. 531)
questions.quote: The most serious complication of polycystic kidney disease is ESRD, which is managed with dialysis or transplant.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client newly diagnosed with polycystic kidney disease is adjusting to the illness. What should the nurse include in the discussions?
questions.rationale: Adult polycystic kidney disease is autosomal dominant, so the client and extended family should have genetic counseling. Fluid restriction is unnecessary, and hypertension is more likely.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q814 (PDF p. 1048)
questions.quote: Because of this, the client and the extended family should have genetic counseling.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client returns from a left nephrectomy. Which assessment is MOST important to do hourly?
questions.rationale: Hourly urine output shows how well the remaining kidney is working and detects renal failure early. Pain, vital signs, and coughing and deep breathing are also monitored. The client is NPO at first.
explanations: The client is NPO at first.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q364 (PDF p. 532)
questions.quote: After nephrectomy, it is imperative to measure the urine output on an hourly basis.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Aling Nena, 58, has chronic kidney disease and gets hemodialysis through an AV fistula in her right arm.
questions.stem: Which action protects Aling Nena's AV fistula?
options: Take BP on the right arm
Draw blood from the right arm
Check for a thrill and bruit
questions.rationale: The nurse palpates for a thrill and auscultates for a bruit every 4 hours. No BP readings, venipunctures, or IV lines go on the fistula arm.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q375 (PDF p. 543)
questions.quote: The nurse should implement the following to protect the fistula: palpate for thrills and auscultate for a bruit every 4 hours

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Aling Nena, 58, has chronic kidney disease and gets hemodialysis through an AV fistula in her right arm.
questions.stem: Which statement by Aling Nena about her fistula shows a need for MORE teaching?
options: 'I won't carry heavy bags on that arm.'
questions.rationale: Clients avoid sleeping on the access arm, carrying heavy objects with it, or compressing it, and do routine range-of-motion exercises.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1082 (PDF p. 1364)
questions.quote: avoiding sleeping with the body weight on the extremity with the access site

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Aling Nena, 58, has chronic kidney disease and gets hemodialysis through an AV fistula in her right arm.
questions.stem: Aling Nena asks how often hemodialysis is done. What is the typical schedule?
questions.rationale: Typical hemodialysis is 3 to 4 hours, 3 days a week, adjusted for body size, dialyzer type, blood flow, and client preference.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q672 (PDF p. 892)
questions.quote: The typical schedule for hemodialysis is 3 to 4 hours of treatment 3 days per week.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Aling Nena, 58, has chronic kidney disease and gets hemodialysis through an AV fistula in her right arm.
questions.stem: What should Aling Nena record daily to monitor her fluid status between treatments?
questions.rationale: Fluid status between treatments is tracked by daily intake and output and weight. Ideally she gains no more than 0.5 kg a day.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q676 (PDF p. 896)
questions.quote: This can be done by recording intake and output and measuring weight on a daily basis.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Aling Nena, 58, has chronic kidney disease and gets hemodialysis through an AV fistula in her right arm.
questions.stem: Which weight gain between dialysis sessions shows Aling Nena is following her diet and fluid limits?
questions.rationale: A limit of about 1 to 1.5 kg between treatments helps prevent the hypotension that occurs when large fluid volumes are removed during dialysis.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1381 (PDF p. 1684)
questions.quote: usually a limit of 1 to 1.5 kg of weight gain between dialysis treatments helps prevent hypotension

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Aling Nena, 58, has chronic kidney disease and gets hemodialysis through an AV fistula in her right arm.
questions.stem: Aling Nena is on a fluid restriction. Which dessert choice shows she understands?
questions.rationale: Anything liquid at room temperature counts as fluid, such as gelatin, sherbet, and ice cream. Avoiding hidden fluids lets her drink more to ease thirst.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q665 (PDF p. 884)
questions.quote: Dietary fluid includes anything that is liquid at room temperature.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Aling Nena, 58, has chronic kidney disease and gets hemodialysis through an AV fistula in her right arm.
questions.stem: Aling Nena has itching from uremia. Which skin care item should she AVOID?
questions.rationale: Perfumes and alcohol dry the skin and worsen itching. Mild soap, bath oil, and lotion reduce dryness.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q666 (PDF p. 885)
questions.quote: Products that contain perfumes or alcohol increase skin dryness and pruritus and these should be avoided.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Aling Nena, 58, has chronic kidney disease and gets hemodialysis through an AV fistula in her right arm.
questions.stem: Aling Nena is on a protein-restricted diet. Which foods are INCOMPLETE proteins?
questions.rationale: Nuts and grains are incomplete proteins. Meat, fish, milk, and eggs are complete proteins.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1353 (PDF p. 1656)
questions.quote: Nuts and grains are the only options that are not complete proteins.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with CKD is told he needs hemodialysis and says angrily, 'I'll never be the same.' What is his PRIMARY concern?
questions.rationale: Clients may become angry over the permanence of CKD. Physical and lifestyle changes can cause an altered body image.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q809 (PDF p. 1043)
questions.quote: the client may experience an altered body image.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Mang Ben, 48, has calcium oxalate kidney stones.
questions.stem: Which list of high-oxalate foods shows Mang Ben understood the teaching?
questions.rationale: High-oxalate foods include beets, spinach, rhubarb, black tea, cocoa, nuts, okra, and chocolate. He should also drink up to 3000 mL a day unless restricted.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q378 (PDF p. 547)
questions.quote: Food items that are high in oxalate include beets, spinach, rhubarb, black tea

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Mang Ben, 48, has calcium oxalate kidney stones.
questions.stem: Mang Ben's passed stone is calcium oxalate. Which food is BEST to avoid?
questions.rationale: Foods that raise urinary oxalate include spinach, rhubarb, strawberries, chocolate, nuts, beets, tea, and okra.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q633 (PDF p. 851)
questions.quote: Foods that raise urinary oxalate excretion and predispose to stone formation include spinach, rhubarb, strawberries, chocolate, wheat bran, nuts, beets

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Mang Ben, 48, has calcium oxalate kidney stones.
questions.stem: Two hours after morphine, Mang Ben says, 'I'm scared to death the pain will come back.' What is the PRIORITY concern?
questions.rationale: Anticipating recurring pain produces anxiety and threatens psychological integrity. No data suggest a lack of knowledge or poor coping.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q935 (PDF p. 1179)
questions.quote: The anticipation of the recurring pain produces anxiety and threatens the client’s psychological integrity.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client has uric acid stones. Which food should the nurse teach him to avoid?
questions.rationale: Purines are broken down into uric acid. Organ meats such as liver are high in purines and are limited.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q642 (PDF p. 860)
questions.quote: the nurse instructs the client to avoid foods that contain high amounts of purines because these foods contain a high concentration of uric acid.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How many glasses of water a day should a client with a nephrostomy tube drink at home?
questions.rationale: About 2000 mL a day (6 to 8 glasses) dilutes particles that could form stones and flushes the kidney and the tube.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q613 (PDF p. 826)
questions.quote: The nurse encourages the client to take in 2000 mL of fluid per day, which is roughly equivalent to 6 to 8 glasses of water.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client is admitted for ureterolithotomy. Which assessment shows readiness for surgery?
questions.rationale: As with any surgery, the client should know the procedure, the expected outcome, postoperative routines, and expected pain management.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q815 (PDF p. 1049)
questions.quote: The client should have an understanding of the same items as are required for any surgery

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with prostatitis asks why a stool softener is ordered. Which reply is BEST?
questions.rationale: Stool softeners prevent constipation, which is painful with an inflamed prostate. They do not reduce swelling directly.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q652 (PDF p. 870)
questions.quote: Stool softeners are prescribed for the client with prostatitis to prevent constipation, which can be painful.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Mang Tonyo, 68, had a transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) for benign prostatic hyperplasia.
questions.stem: What should the nurse include in Mang Tonyo's discharge teaching?
options: Lift up to 20 kg after 2 weeks
questions.rationale: He reports infection, bleeding, more pain, or obstruction. Strenuous activity and lifting more than about 20 pounds (9 kg) are avoided for 4 to 6 weeks.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q655 (PDF p. 873)
questions.quote: The client should notify the primary health care provider if there are any signs/symptoms of infection, bleeding, increased pain, or urinary obstruction.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Mang Tonyo, 68, had a transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) for benign prostatic hyperplasia.
questions.stem: Which statement by Mang Tonyo shows a need for MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Straining during defecation is avoided to prevent bleeding. Prune juice helps, and he drinks 6 to 8 glasses of fluid a day.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1066 (PDF p. 1348)
questions.quote: Straining during defecation is avoided to prevent bleeding.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Mang Tonyo, 68, had a transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) for benign prostatic hyperplasia.
questions.stem: Mang Tonyo has continuous bladder irrigation. Which drainage color shows the flow rate is adequate?
questions.rationale: The irrigation is adjusted to keep drainage clear pale yellow or slightly pink. It is increased if drainage is cherry colored or has clots.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1238 (PDF p. 1531)
questions.quote: it is increased or decreased to maintain urine that is a clear, pale yellow color or has just a slight pink tinge.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Mang Tonyo, 68, had a transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) for benign prostatic hyperplasia.
questions.stem: Which drainage color should the nurse report to the provider?
questions.rationale: Bright red drainage may mean active bleeding. Pale pink is expected. Dark pink means the irrigation rate should be increased.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1374 (PDF p. 1677)
questions.quote: Bright red bleeding should be reported because it could indicate complications related to active bleeding.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Mang Tonyo, 68, had a transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) for benign prostatic hyperplasia.
questions.stem: What urine color should Mang Tonyo expect for several days after going home?
questions.rationale: Urine is pink-tinged for several days. Dark red must be corrected, clear urine is not yet expected, and cloudy urine may mean infection.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1460 (PDF p. 1769)
questions.quote: The client should expect that the urine will be pink-tinged for several days after this procedure.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client asks how the prostate is removed in TURP. Through which route?
questions.rationale: TURP uses a resectoscope passed through the urethra. Suprapubic and retropubic approaches use a lower abdominal incision, and the perineal approach goes between scrotum and anus.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1386 (PDF p. 1689)
questions.quote: A TURP is done through the urethra.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: At a prostate screening clinic, which sign of prostatism should the nurse ask about?
questions.rationale: Prostatism includes a weaker, intermittent stream, hesitancy, inability to stop quickly, a sense of incomplete emptying, and nocturia.
explanations: Inability to stop is a sign.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1377 (PDF p. 1680)
questions.quote: hesitancy in beginning the flow of urine, inability to stop urinating quickly

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with renal cell carcinoma of the left kidney (right kidney normal) fears needing dialysis. What should the nurse say FIRST?
questions.rationale: The client needs support and reassurance that a normally functioning remaining kidney can fully meet the body's metabolic needs.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q998 (PDF p. 1249)
questions.quote: the remaining kidney should be able to fully meet the body’s metabolic needs as long as it has normal function.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with nephrotic syndrome says, 'Why bother with my diet? Nothing I do will fix my kidneys.' What is the MOST appropriate concern?
questions.rationale: Powerlessness is the belief that one's actions will not affect the outcome. Nephrotic syndrome is progressive, so the client may feel this way.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q997 (PDF p. 1248)
questions.quote: Powerlessness is present when the client believes that personal actions will not affect an outcome in any significant way.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After 2 days of care for nephrotic syndrome, which result shows the SMALLEST improvement?
questions.rationale: Therapy aims to heal the leaking glomerular membrane. The 0.1 g/dL rise in serum albumin is the smallest change.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1208 (PDF p. 1500)
questions.quote: The least amount of improvement is in the serum albumin

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which statement by a client with acute kidney injury shows a need for MORE teaching about high-quality protein?
questions.rationale: Complete proteins come from animal sources such as eggs, chicken, meat, and fish. Plant foods give incomplete proteins. With protein limited, the protein eaten should be high quality.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q656 (PDF p. 874)
questions.quote: High-quality or complete proteins come from animal sources and include such foods as eggs, chicken, meat, and fish.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client recovering from acute kidney injury should limit which dietary factor?
questions.rationale: The kidneys excrete most potassium. In kidney failure, potassium is restricted (30 to 50 mEq/day), and dialysis is the main way to remove it.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1210 (PDF p. 1503)
questions.quote: In the client with renal failure, potassium intake must be restricted as much as possible (30 to 50 mEq/day).

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with glomerulonephritis is at risk for acute kidney injury. Which complication should the nurse monitor for?
questions.rationale: Intrarenal AKI from glomerulonephritis shows hypertension, tachycardia, oliguria, edema, and other signs of fluid overload. Prerenal AKI shows low output and low CVP.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1540 (PDF p. 1851)
questions.quote: This form of acute kidney injury is commonly manifested by hypertension, tachycardia, oliguria, lethargy, edema, and other signs of fluid overload.
